sources.title: The Eiffel Tower, now the most photographed structure on Earth, was built in 1889 as a temporary centerpiece for the Paris World's Fair — meant to be dismantled after 20 years — and was saved from demolition in 1909 only because Gustave Eiffel himself arranged for the French military to use its iron lattice as a radio antenna for transmitting wireless signals across long distances

excerpts.text: The Eiffel Tower was never meant to last. It was built as a temporary attraction for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris, and the deal was explicit: it would stand for twenty years, and then, in 1909, it would be dismantled and sold for scrap iron.
